Abstract.AbstractText: Rearrangement of the ALK gene and overexpression of ALK seems to occur very rarely in neuroendocrine lung tumors, with only 3 cases of atypical carcinoid and 1 large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) reported in detail until now.(1,2,3,4) Here, we report a case of an ALK-positive neuroendocrine lung tumor showing a variable phenotype during the course of treatment. A pulmonary lesion with mediastinal adenopathies was detected in a 69-year-old, non-smoking female of Turkish origin during work-up for back pain. A very small amount of tumoral tissue was obtained through fine needle aspiration of a lymph node and stainings performed on paraffin-embedded tissue showed a very limited amount of tumoral tissue with a well-differentiated cytological aspect with regular nuclei.
